name: Wachsmut von Mühlhausen
credit: Wachsmut von Mühlhausen, miniature in the Codex Manesse (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848), c. 1300–1340 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Wachsmut von Mühlhausen was a minnesinger of about 1200 whose songs are preserved in the Codex Manesse.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: Wishes
poems.author: Wachsmut von Mühlhausen
poems.text:
Where did ever mortal eye
See two lovelier cheeks displayed?
Lily-white, without a lie,
Sweetly, featly are they made.
Long and pale and gold's her hair.
If hers and mine the whole realm were,—
I would give no one else a share!

From my lady's lips a kiss
Softer burns than any blaze.
Should she grant a mortal this,
He'd be happy all his days.
Help me wish now, all of you,
That I get a kiss from her!
Then—something else I'll wish thereto!
